title: Police screening for massage establishment licences under the Massage Establishment Act
asked: Mr Foo Cexiang asked whether the Singapore Police Force will consider enhancing the screening process for Massage Establishment Act licence applicants, especially for association with persons who breached MEA licensing conditions or are facing ongoing investigations.
response: Ms Sim Ann said MHA amended the Massage Establishment Act in 2017 to expand Police consideration to responsible officers and persons with substantial interest, control or direction over the business. The Police can refuse a licence if these persons are not fit and proper, and assess criminal antecedents, past breaches of ME regulations, ongoing investigations, and law and order or social disamenity concerns. If association with others who previously breached ME licensing conditions could cause law and order concerns, the Police can also refuse a licence. In reply to a supplementary question, she said the plan is for these considerations to apply to a new category of MEs not currently licensed under the Act.

key_points.point: MHA amended the Massage Establishment Act in 2017 to expand Police consideration of licence applications.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: In 2017, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) amended the Massage Establishment Act (MEA)

key_points.point: The expanded consideration covers responsible officers and persons with substantial interest, control or direction over the business.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: to expand the Police's consideration when assessing massage establishment (ME) licence applications

key_points.point: Responsible officers include business partners in a partnership, governing body members in an unincorporated association, and directors or similar officers in a corporate body.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: Responsible officers include business partners if the business entity is a partnership

key_points.point: The Police can refuse an ME licence if these persons are not fit and proper.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: If these persons are not fit and proper, the Police can refuse to grant an ME licence.

key_points.point: Fitness and propriety assessment includes criminal antecedents, past breaches of ME regulations, and ongoing investigations.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: the Police would consider, but is not limited to, criminal antecedents, past breaches of ME regulations, if the person is facing ongoing investigations

key_points.point: Association with others who previously breached ME licensing conditions can also lead to refusal if it could cause law and order concerns.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: If the Police assess that a person's association with others who had previously breached ME licensing conditions could cause law and order concerns

key_points.point: The considerations are planned to apply to a new category of MEs not currently licensed under the Act.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann

left_open: Whether any further enhancement of the screening process, beyond the 2017 amendments, is planned.
supplementary: Whether the same Police screening considerations will apply to a new category of massage establishments not currently licensed under the Act.
